media:group.media:title: U.S. Spacewalk Preview News Conference (Oct. 20, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
We're giving a preview of two upcoming spacewalks on Oct. 29 and Nov. 5 to finish installing solar arrays that will provide more power to the International Space Station.
NASA astronaut Anil Menon and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk will participate in both spacewalks. The spacewalks will be the 285th and 286th conducted in support of space station assembly, maintenance, and upgrades.
NASA participants in the news conference include: - Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager, Low Earth Orbit Program - Garrett Hehn, spacewalk flight director, Flight Operations Directorate
Learn more about the spacewalks: https://go.nasa.gov/4yRBm97 Learn more about International Space Station operations and research: https://www.nasa.gov/station

entry.title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Postflight News Conference (Oct. 15, 2026)

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Postflight News Conference (Oct. 15, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
After spending over seven months in space, members of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 will discuss their mission aboard the International Space Station during a news conference at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.
NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev returned to Earth on Oct. 8, after spending 237 days living and working in orbit. (Adenot will return to Europe and not be available during the news conference.)
Learn more about Crew-12's science and technology research: https://go.nasa.gov/4jdAre7
Watch Crew-12's return to Earth: https://youtube.com/live/x6p9Ri0DlNE
Read more about Crew-12's return and today's event: https://go.nasa.gov/3UikER9

entry.title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Rendezvous and Docking

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Rendezvous and Docking
media:group.media:description:
Following a successful launch on Oct. 13, 2026, an uncrewed SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft will plan to rendezvous with and dock to the International Space Station. The spacecraft, which is carrying over 6,300 pounds of supplies, is scheduled to dock autonomously at about 10:30 a.m. EDT (1430 UTC).
In addition to cargo for the crew aboard the space station, Dragon will deliver several new science experiments that could help restore vision for people on Earth with artificial eye retinas, develop more realistic heart tissue models for disease research, and identify new treatment targets for diseases like Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and multiple sclerosis.
Dragon is scheduled to remain at the space station for one month before undocking and splashing down off the coast of California.
Learn more about the mission: https://www.nasa.gov/general/nasas-spacex-35th-commercial-resupply-mission-overview/
Learn more about International Space Station operations and research: https://www.nasa.gov/station

entry.title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Launch

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX 35th Commercial Resupply Services Launch
media:group.media:description:
Tune in as a new shipment of science and supplies lifts off to the International Space Station.
NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT (1033 UTC), Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next cargo launch of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft to the space station. Dragon will lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida and is scheduled to dock autonomously at around 11:00 a.m. EDT (1500 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 15, to the space-facing port of the station’s Harmony module.
Learn more about the mission and the launch timeline: https://go.nasa.gov/3WhHUPG

entry.title: NASA's Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 24 Departure

media:group.media:title: NASA's Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 24 Departure
media:group.media:description:
Watch Northrop Grumman’s Cygnus XL spacecraft undock and depart from the International Space Station.
Flight controllers on the ground will send commands for the space station’s Canadarm2 robotic arm to detach the Cygnus XL spacecraft from the Unity module’s Earth-facing port and maneuver it into position for release at 12:45 p.m. EDT (1645 UTC).
This Cygnus XL previously delivered more than 11,000 pounds of supplies, science experiments, and other cargo to the space station.
Learn more about this NASA commercial resupply mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-northrop-grumman-crs-24/

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Re-Entry & Splashdown
media:group.media:description:
Welcome Crew-12 back to Earth with us!
NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev are scheduled to splash down off the coast of California at 11:34 a.m. EDT (1534 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 8.
We'll have live coverage from re-entry to recovery. Crew-12 spent 235 days on the International Space Station and orbited Earth nearly 3,800 times.
Learn more about what Crew-12 studied during their time in space: https://go.nasa.gov/4z5jVl6 Get the latest updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Undocking
media:group.media:description:
Watch the four members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission — NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev — set off to return to Earth. The SpaceX Dragon spacecraft will undock from the International Space Station at approximately 8:05 a.m. EDT (1205 UTC).
Splashdown is scheduled to occur off the coast of California on Thursday, Oct. 8 at 11:34 a.m. EDT (1534 UTC).
During their nearly eight months aboard the space station, Crew-12 conducted hundreds of hours of scientific research. Their work included testing stem cell production for cell‑based therapies, examining how physical characteristics may affect blood flow during spaceflight, and demonstrating the on‑demand generation of IV fluid for future missions.
Learn more about the Crew-12 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-12/ Follow the latest Crew-12 updates: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/crew-12/

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 Hatch Close
media:group.media:description:
Watch as NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev begin final preparations for their return to Earth aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft.
After the four enter the spacecraft, the hatch is scheduled to close at 6:20 a.m. EDT (1020 UTC). The Dragon is scheduled to undock at 8:05 a.m. EDT (1205 UTC).
Crew-12’s splashdown is targeted for Thursday, Oct. 8 at 11:34 a.m. EDT (1534 UTC).
Learn more about the Crew-12 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-12/ Follow the latest Crew-12 updates: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/crew-12/

entry.title: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Farewell and International Space Station Change of Command

media:group.media:title: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Farewell and International Space Station Change of Command
media:group.media:description:
Watch as the members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission – NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev – sum up their experiences aboard the International Space Station and say goodbye to the space station crew. Meir will also transfer command of the orbiting laboratory to Roscosmos cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov.
Learn more about Crew-12: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-12/

entry.title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Arrival & Welcome Remarks

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Arrival & Welcome Remarks
media:group.media:description:
Watch as four explorers arrive at the International Space Station.
After lifting off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Thursday, Oct. 1, at 11:10 a.m. EDT (1510 UTC), Crew-13's spacecraft is scheduled to dock at the orbiting lab at 7 p.m. EDT (2300 UTC), with hatches opening at about 8:45 p.m. EDT (0045 UTC Oct. 2). The crew will also give welcome remarks around 9:20 p.m. EDT (0120 UTC Oct. 2).
NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov will spend the next several months in low Earth orbit on NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission.
While there, they will conduct various science experiments and technology demonstrations to benefit life on Earth and in orbit, furthering humanity's journey back to the Moon, to Mars, and beyond.
Learn more about the Crew-13 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-13/ Read daily updates from the space station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

entry.title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Postlaunch News Conference (Oct. 1, 2026)

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Postlaunch News Conference (Oct. 1, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
After the successful launch of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission, leaders discuss the mission and answer questions from media.
Participants include: - NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman - Dr. Lori Glaze, associate administrator, Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters - Dana Weigel, manager, Low Earth Orbit Program, NASA Johnson - Mathieu Caron, director, Astronauts, Life Sciences, and Space Medicine, CSA - Julianna Scheiman, director, NASA Science and Dragon Programs, SpaceX
NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov launched to the International Space Station (ISS) at 11:10 a.m. EDT (1510 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 1. They are expected to arrive at the space station around 7 p.m. EDT (2300 UTC).
While there, the Crew-13 members will conduct various experiments and technology demonstrations to benefit life on Earth and in orbit, furthering our journey back to the Moon, to Mars, and beyond.
Learn more about the ISS: https://www.nasa.gov/reference/international-space-station/ Get updates on Crew-13: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/crew-13/

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Launch
media:group.media:description:
Four new crew members are heading to the International Space Station!
NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov are lifting off aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft to spend several months living, working, and conducting scientific research in low Earth orbit.
NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission is scheduled to lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida at 11:10 a.m. EDT (1510 UTC) on Thursday, Oct. 1. The four members of Crew-13 will arrive at the space station later that day.
Learn more about the Crew-13 mission: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-13/ Get daily updates from the station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

entry.title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Prelaunch News Conference (Sept. 30, 2026)

media:group.media:title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Prelaunch News Conference (Sept. 30, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
Mission experts give a preview of NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station ahead of its launch.
Participants include: - Dr. Lori Glaze, associate administrator, Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters - Dana Weigel, manager, Low Earth Orbit Program, NASA Johnson - Mathieu Caron, director, Astronauts, Life Sciences, and Space Medicine, CSA - William Gerstenmaier, vice president, Build and Flight Reliability, SpaceX
Crew-13 is scheduled to launch at 11:10 a.m. EDT (1510 UTC), Thursday, Oct. 1, from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, with docking planned for about 7 p.m. EDT (2300 UTC).
The SpaceX Dragon spacecraft will carry Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov to the International Space Station for a long-duration science mission.
Learn more about Crew-13: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-13

media:group.media:title: Space Station Operations Update (Sept. 28, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
Leaders from NASA and Boeing hold a news conference at NASA's Kennedy Space Center to provide updates on Starliner development and plans for crew flights to and from the International Space Station.
Briefing participants include:
* NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman * Dana Weigel, manager, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program * Woody Hoburg, NASA astronaut * John Mulholland, vice president and program manager, Boeing Commercial Crew
Learn more about the Commercial Crew Program: https://www.nasa.gov/commercialcrew Get daily updates from the station: https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/

media:group.media:title: Artemis Acceleration (Oct. 23, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
Tune in as agency leaders provide an update on NASA's plans to return American astronauts to the surface of the Moon by 2028.
Participants include: - NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman - NASA Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya - Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager
As part of a Golden Age of innovation and exploration, NASA will send Artemis astronauts on increasingly difficult missions near the lunar South Pole to explore more of the Moon than ever before. In addition to providing economic benefits and advancing scientific discovery through its Moon missions, NASA will establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface and build on the agency’s foundation for the first crewed mission to Mars.
More about the Artemis program: https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/artemis/
